Before the 63-year-old founder was ousted, the company did try to hire an external number two, according to a person familiar with the search. It was difficult to find candidates, though, because none wanted to work in Huang’s shadow. The Huang hangover might still be a problem even after he’s gone. There’s a Slack group at the company, for instance, titled “Stand with Jensen,” and people familiar with the search process estimate there are fewer than 10 people in the world truly capable of running the company. The next Nvidia CEO doesn’t just have to keep its own products shipping on time. The person who takes the top job also has to keep the entire industry alive. There’s really no replacing him . What they're saying: While the investigation remains ongoing, officials said the Atlantic Asphalt tanker appeared to have lost control, causing it to collide with the cruise ship. As passengers were disembarking after the collision, the cruise ship began to sink and eventually toppled over and flipped — leaving people in the cold water. Video from the scene shows passengers, in life preservers, swimming in the river toward safety. The first 87 passengers got off while the ship was still afloat, Harbor Police Chief Melanie Montroll said. articles.summary: The FAA on Friday lifted a rare nationwide ground stop that impacted more than 14,500 flights after a major outage affecting the US’ air communications system. US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed “an incredibly old air traffic control system,” and said the government didn’t suspect any nefarious causes, such as a terrorist or cyber attack. He said the issues were connected to old equipment that was overloaded, and that flights should start taking off again over the next day. “Hopefully tomorrow, we are going to start to see far better movement,” he said, while trying to reassure travelers that the US remains “the safest system in the world.” The stoppage, which lasted more than four hours, caused widespread disruption and prompted shares in airlines to drop. American Airlines shares dropped more than 2% in after-hours trading, while United shares fell 1.6%. Those airlines are now navigating thousands of rebookings and frustrated passengers. articles.author: Lauren Hartley
articles.summary: Andreas Gebert / Andreas Gebert, Reuters More than 720,000 BMWs are being recalled over fears they could catch fire—even while parked with their engines off. Officials are urging owners of the 14 affected models to park outside. “If you have one of these vehicles, you should park your vehicle outside and away from buildings and other vehicles until the vehicle is repaired,” the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said in a statement. The issue stems from an improperly sealed electrical connector on the water pump. If exposed to water, it could short-circuit and spark a fire. “Over time, due to material degradation at the connector, this could allow moisture to enter the pump and lead to the possibility of a short circuit,” the document states. “This could increase the risk of a thermal event and, in rare cases, a fire.” Ten incidents have been reported so far. BMW has not yet identified a remedy. Letters notifying affected owners will be sent in December. This is the second recall for these vehicles. They were previously recalled in 2024 over a separate water pump issue. Read it at TMZ Read more at The Daily Beast.

In addition to lowering the cost of commercial space launches and providing satellite capabilities to Ukraine through Starlink, SpaceX is increasingly critical to US strategic competition in space, without which “NASA would still need Russia to carry astronauts to the ISS,” a Bloomberg columnist argued. “That’s something to keep in mind as legislators sharpen their knives .” — Brendan Ruberry
